summary_paragraph: The patient with recent Roux-en-Y gastric bypass reversal was admitted to the surgery service for nausea with inability to tolerate oral intake and associated dehydration with dizziness and bilious emesis despite home ondansetron. She was treated with intravenous fluids and symptom management, remained afebrile and hemodynamically stable without evidence of infection or bleeding, and her labs stayed stable. Nausea was noted to be worse with protein shakes; diet was adjusted from bariatric Stage 3 toward a mechanical soft/Stage 4 soft mechanical approach, which she tolerated (broth, cream of wheat, water) without recurrent vomiting. She received education on the soft mechanical diet and was discharged home ambulatory with instructions to crush pills, avoid NSAIDs/aspirin, use ondansetron and newly prescribed prochlorperazine as needed for nausea, and follow postoperative activity and wound-care precautions.
